pairs.question: De ambitu vero, quid interest an de maiestate?
pairs.answer: Ad rem nihil; alterum enim non attigisti, alteram auxisti.
pairs.derivation: Cicero quotes the projected question of his interlocutor Appius. Framing speech-tag 'inquies' (set between the two halves of the quoted question) is dropped; the two contiguous halves '"De ambitu vero, quid interest," ... "an de maiestate?"' are quoted as one interrogative. The answer begins immediately at Cicero's reply 'ad rem nihil' (capitalized). I end the answer at 'auxisti' — the operative direct answer (the difference is nothing to the point: ambitus he did not touch, maiestas he aggravated) — and cut before the digression 'verumtamen ea est maiestas, ut Sulla voluit...' which turns from answering to general comment. The original separates these clauses with semicolons; terminal semicolon normalized to a full stop.

pairs.question: Quid tu igitur, si affuisses?
pairs.answer: Rem probassem, de tempore, nihil te invito, nihil sine consilio egissem tuo.
pairs.derivation: Cicero poses a question to himself in Appius's voice ('In hoc autem mihi illud occurrit: "quid tu igitur, si affuisses?"'). The narration 'In hoc autem mihi illud occurrit' is dropped as framing; the quoted interrogative is kept verbatim, first word capitalized. The answer is the contiguous reply 'rem probassem... egissem tuo' (capitalized), ending at the full stop before 'Vides sudare me iamdudum...', where Cicero turns from answering to commenting on his own difficulty.
